headline: Microsoft Will Offer Buyouts to 60,000 Employees
author: Kanebridge

paragraphs.text: , the company said on Monday. Around 60,000 employees are eligible for the program, according to a person familiar with the matter. K.

S. “The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we’re evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter,” Amy Coleman, Microsoft’s chief people officer, said in a message sent to employees. Microsoft said the program was “time-limited” and would provide eligible employees with financial support and career planning resources.

Coleman said eligible employees would receive an email link with their offer details in the next few hours. Microsoft in April announced a voluntary retirement program, which offered around 8,600 employees buyouts, the person familiar with the matter said, and more than 30% accepted the offer. The company expects a far lower percentage to accept the latest buyouts, the person said.

Microsoft employed 223,000 employees as of the end of June. The voluntary retirement program was part of a broader shift by Microsoft to alter its performance system and how it awards bonuses and stock options, according to a memo to employees from Coleman viewed by The Wall Street Journal at the time. Microsoft earlier this year announced 3,200 job cuts in its Xbox videogames division.
